payload.title: Assignment is the request between agents
payload.description:
When one agent needs another's work (the fact-checker needs a source found, the copy editor needs a figure), it creates an `Assignment` for that responsibility on the subject, through the gate. `Assignment` already exists with claim, release, complete, cancel, reopen and events; make its kind any responsibility from the catalog. Its creation wakes the responsible agent; the wake key is the claim; completion writes the result on the subject and closes the Assignment, which wakes the asker. A person creates the same record from the newsroom. An Assignment is never a Message.

**Acceptance criteria**
- An agent's request appears on the subject as an Assignment with who asked and why.
- The responsible agent runs once for it.
- Completion wakes the asker; a failure is recorded on the Assignment and raises one flag.
- Every behaviour change ships with narrative Gherkin specs (below).

**Gherkin features needed**
- assignment-handoff.feature: the fact-checker asks for a source and research runs once; the result returns to the Story; a person files the same request; a failed assignment is not retried by itself.

**Infrastructure as code touched:** None.

**Part of:** Work items and handoffs between agents and people. Slice code F1 in `docs/design/always-on-agents-architecture.md` (section 12).
**Standing rules:** no fallbacks, no workarounds, no interim systems, no arbitrary caps; no text in DynamoDB; indexes over scans; no AppSync subscriptions; nothing created by hand in AWS; no real email addresses in specs or fixtures; status shown as words and marks, never colour alone.
